newsitem.title: USA: Northeast says Conn. debt relief difficult.
newsitem.headline: Northeast says Conn. debt relief difficult.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Monday that Connecticut's draft bill on electricity deregulation paints a "difficult" scenario for recovery of stranded costs.
"This is a complex, complicated bill," Northeast spokeswoman Myra Humphries told Reuters.
"The treatment of stranded costs is more difficult than that enacted in other states." She did not elaborate.
Stranded costs are typically linked to power plants built prior to market deregulation, when their costs could be passed on through the rates utilities charged to their customers.

In the revised draft of Connecticut House Bill 6776 released last Friday, there is a provision for the securitization of up to 65 percent of above-market nuclear investment and 100 percent of regulatory assets.
Securitization involves issuing bonds to cover the debt or stranded costs.
Northeast Utilities, weighed down by heavy debt tied to its three idled Millstone nuclear power plants in Waterford, Conn., has estimated its stranded costs at about $3 billion.
The amended bill would not allow a utility to securitize any nuclear investment that was not currently in operation.

"In our opinion, this provision could make it more difficult for (Northeast) to reach the legislation's mandated near-term rate reduction (of 10 percent) as some timing differences will likely arise due to the current restart schedule of the company's Millstone nuclear units and associated regulatory lag," HSBC James Capel wrote in a research report.
Northeast would be eligible to securitize about $1.4 billion in above-market nuclear investment.
Under the current version of the bill, Northeast would not be allowed to securitize its stranded costs until each of its nuclear units has been returned to service.
Northeast has said it intends to have its three Millstone plants ready for restart by early 1998, pending approval by federal regulators.
"More positively, the amended draft included a true-up on stranded cost recovery in 2002 in lieu of the 2005 date suggested in the original draft," HSBC James Capel wrote.
The amended draft bill is expected to go to the House floor for deliberations this week.
